notes:
Snapshot from calls/threads and engineering notes:
- Company: mobile ad-personalization & recommendations (SDK in Go + edge gateways).
- Primary ask: sub-60ms p99 for 1-2k daily active queries per user, overall 300-600 QPS steady, spikes to 1.5k QPS.
- Workload mix: 70% short prompts for reranking/top-N (50-200 tokens), 20% chat snippets (context window ~512 tokens), 10% embeddings offline.
- Cost sensitivity: unit cost must be < $0.0009/token equivalent for reranking path to keep CPM economics. CFO watching ARR/unit.
- Model preference: open Llama-family variants + smaller instruct models; willing to try 8-bit quantized variants. Want Redwood Optimize recommendations on quant profiles.
- Perf needs: p50 < 18ms, p95 < 30ms, p99 < 60ms for rerank endpoint. Throughput targets require batching window ~5-10ms or continuous batching with dynamic latency cap.
- Operational constraints: VPC-only control plane, EU data residency for user contexts, KMS-managed keys, full audit logs for retraining dataset pipeline.
- Reliability: automatic fallback to cached top-N responses; want canary rollouts and instant fallback to cheaper variant when latency spike detected.
- Integrations: Current infra uses Redis prefix cache for conversational state; wants KV cache coalescing and Redis-compatible cache TTL semantics.
- Quote from Eng lead Priya: "We can sacrifice a few points of quality if we cut inference cost in half — but p99 is non-negotiable."
- Action items: provide perf bench harness, sample quantization tradeoff report, map of expected token distributions, sample canary rollout config.
- Stubs/refs: ff_2026-03-02_9a3b2c (recording), drive:/PulseQuarry/Redwood-PoC-Plan-v2.pdf, thread-CAf9x3k_20260304 (pricing questions).
use_case_summary: PulseQuarry builds millisecond-scale personalization pipelines embedded in mobile SDKs. They need Redwood to validate whether Dedicated + Optimize can meet tight p99 latency targets while reducing per-request cost via batching, prefix/KV caching, and 8-bit quantization. Priority items: perf benchmarking for 3 workload profiles (rerank, chat snippet, embedding precompute), recommendations for batch size/latency tradeoffs, suggested quantization profiles and fallbacks, and a POC runbook showing cost delta between standard vs quantized serving. SE asked to instrument end-to-end benchmark that includes network hop (VPC peering) and cache warm-up behavior.
